scope: Read-only source diagnosis for the T87, T89, and T90 native receipt acceptance gap; no native execution or product patch.

signing_door: The owned native harness already has a localhost page and a separate extension side panel. localhost is in the WebMCP runtime allowlist, and webmcp-bridge.content.ts runs on it.

An actual page posts {__matrx_webmcp_call:true,callId,toolName,args} to its window; the existing content script sends {__matrx:true,kind:'webmcp:call',payload:{callId,toolName,args}} to the service worker. background/bootstrap.ts checks the sender origin and calls handleWebmcpCall.

For a registered read-tier tool, handleWebmcpCall runs the handler, then starts both product emitPartialReceipt and emitCompletedReceipt with origin 'webmcp'. Both use buildReceipt, which uses getOrCreateDeviceKey and Ed25519, then appendReceipt to chrome.storage.local['matrx.audit.log']. These emissions are fire-and-forget, so the call response alone is not a persistence oracle.

page_message.callId: unique opaque ID generated by the native runner

exact_minimal_call.expected_page_result: {__matrx_webmcp_result:true,callId:<same>,ok:true,result:{count,tabs}}; retain no tab URLs or titles in the acceptance report
exact_minimal_call.preconditions: Exact immutable development artifact and owned disposable Chrome profile verified by the existing runner; actual admin Settings identity verified; localhost content script loaded; no optional permission or action confirmation required for read-tier list_open_tabs. Do not send webmcp:call directly from an extension page: its sender URL fails the allowlisted-page check.

storage_and_verifier: getRecentReceipts/getReceiptByCallId read the local receipt ring; getPublicKeyById reads matrx.audit.publicKeyHistory under the native Web Lock and permits a pending entry only when it is active.

verifyReceipt imports that historical public JWK and verifies the stored canonical body and Ed25519 signature; a changed body with the same signature returns {valid:false,reason:'signature does not match body — receipt may have been tampered with'}.

The only source-level production caller of verifyReceipt is ToolReceiptDialog, mounted by a chat ToolTimelineRow. Settings RecentReceiptsPanel renders the last 20 receipt rows without a click, verifier result, or import/verify control. No receipt verification runtime message or tool was found in src/lib/messaging, src/lib/background, or src/entrypoints.

minimal_native_proof_if_verifier_is_expo: For T87, send and poll for a completed signed receipt under the old active public ID before the controlled failed rotation; after the separately confirmed rotation, reload and verify that original receipt with the product verifier.

For T89, create a completed receipt under the pre-fault active public ID before the persisted-then-rejected active write; after details-only recovery and reload, verify the old receipt and assert no second rotation.

For T90, create a completed receipt under the original key. Hold the first rotation's active write. Queue a WebMCP read call so its product signer waits on matrx:audit:device-key, and only then queue the second rotation; confirm pending lock order before releasing the first write. The queued signer must capture the first activated public ID before the second rotation takes the lock. After second activation, send another read call and poll for its completed receipt under the second activated public ID. Reload both extension documents and verify all genuine receipts; alter one non-signature body field in a copy of each receipt and require valid:false from the same product verifier. Restore any temporary log mutation in the owned profile.

For each call, wait for chrome.storage.local['matrx.audit.log'] to contain the matching callId, outputHash not 'pending', a nonempty signature, and the expected publicKeyId. Use the actual compiled product verifier from the same immutable artifact in each reloaded extension document for genuine and tampered copies. The WebMCP result is only a handler oracle; the stored signed row and product verifier verdict are the receipt oracles. Report only call IDs, public IDs, counts, booleans, and bounded failure codes.
missing_ui_door: The existing WebMCP path can create genuine receipts, but it does not produce a chat ToolTimelineRow. Therefore its receipts cannot reach ToolReceiptDialog through an existing UI. Settings displays them without invoking verifyReceipt. The exact target artifact does export the production verifier, so a native code-path proof can use that real function without a product UI change.
smallest_legitimate_next_step: Native owner should use target artifact's already-bundled D verifier export from each real reloaded extension document, with product-signed receipts created through the existing WebMCP transport. If dynamic import unexpectedly fails at runtime, actual Chat tool calls and ToolReceiptDialog are the narrow fallback; do not add a test hook or duplicate crypto. No product patch was made here.
